request.description: Characterize official target geometry, analytical IK branch qualification, Jacobian conditioning, and instantiated MuJoCo dynamics before the first policy training run.
request.rationale: The physical model leaves unresolved whether inner-radius targets and joint limits make one branch systematically unsafe, or whether the dominant risk is learned closed-loop hold stability. A reproducible official-annulus characterization separates geometric feasibility from later policy-control failures and determines whether the first training run should cover the full radius range or focus on stabilization.

request.candidates_and_roles: No training candidate exists. Working, best-known, and retained roles are empty.
request.cumulative_resource_use: One completed 2,000-sample Python-module measurement; no training steps and no policy evaluation episodes.
request.current_goal_gap: There is no learned candidate and therefore no measured episode success. The immediate gap is causal: it is unknown whether the eventual shortfall will be dominated by geometric/branch coverage, by finite-time reach and settling, or by instability during the strict uninterrupted hold.
request.current_synthesis: Observed evidence: across 2,000 uniform official-annulus samples, the open-elbow and folded-elbow analytical branches were joint-limit valid in 95.05% and 93.95% of samples. Each branch reached a worst sampled limit margin near -10 degrees. The Jacobian minimum singular value was about 0.0416 m and the maximum condition number about 5.28 for both branches, so the sampled geometry was not near a severe numerical singularity. The instantiated model confirms 2 ms physics, gear 5 actuators, and nonzero generated masses/inertias. Interpretation: joint-limit qualification is a consequential coverage constraint, but the measurement does not identify whether a learned policy can route around invalid branches or whether hold dynamics will dominate failures. Competing explanations remain: (1) the training radius restriction and branch ambiguity cause systematic failures, especially at inner radii and limit-threatening angles; (2) geometry is manageable and the dominant loss is residual velocity/active damping during the 100-step hold. M1 does not measure policy behavior, settling, or success probability, so neither explanation is established.
request.decision_frontier: Before changing the recipe, determine whether a baseline policy's failures are primarily reach/coverage failures or hold-stability failures. Discriminating evidence is a full official-distribution development evaluation with per-episode target radius/angle, first-entry time, maximum held run, interruptions, and minimum/final distance; geometry/coverage dominance predicts failures concentrated at inner radii or limit-threatening angles and often no entry, whereas hold dominance predicts entry followed by interrupted or short holds across feasible geometry.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2-second Cartesian hold. M1 constrains the route to that goal by showing that target geometry and joint limits can invalidate either nominal IK branch for a nontrivial minority of the official distribution, so a successful policy must regulate while respecting branch and limit structure.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Enter goal review and open a bounded baseline-diagnosis inquiry. The first inquiry action should obtain a baseline policy and evaluate it on a shared official-distribution development panel with the existing diagnostics, using the result to choose between full-radius/branch-aware training changes and stabilization-focused method development.
